guarantees.claim: When state_in_sel equals SI_ZERO, state_in is driven to all zeros.
When state_in_sel equals SI_DATA, state_in is driven to the output of aes_transpose(data_in).
For any state_in_sel value not matching SI_ZERO or SI_DATA (including X or undefined), state_in is driven to all zeros.

assumptions.claim: When state_in_sel is SI_DATA, data_in must be free of X's (valid logical value) to avoid state_in becoming X.
assumptions.risk: state_in becomes X, potentially propagating unknown values into the cipher state and corrupting operation.

uncertain_points.claim: The default case zeroes state_in for any state_in_sel not equal to SI_ZERO or SI_DATA. If state_in_sel takes an unexpected value due to a glitch or fault, the state is wiped immediately. It is unclear whether zeroization is an intentional security fallback or an unhandled case that should raise an error.
uncertain_points.cond: state_in_sel takes a value other than SI_ZERO or SI_DATA
uncertain_points.risk: Unintended zeroization could cause functional failure or unexpected clearing of secret state, but might also be a safe security wipe. No error indication is generated.
